parts: Please review the recent notes in shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/susy-positivity/investigations/wilson-loewner/YM. I'd like to discuss the lattice models that were considered, what they are accomplishing, and evaluate whether that is the best path to continue with. I'd like to brainstorm the best way to continue before moving forward, and may use a different model once we've decided on a path forward.

I’ll read the recent YM notes and the surrounding investigation context, then assess what the lattice models establish and which open question would be most useful to tackle next. I’ll keep this to review and discussion.

The notes separate two advances: an explicit positive boundary construction, and a test of whether a few observables can predict the loops accurately. The first looks substantive. The interacting test is unfavorable for the small families tried so far, but its contour steps are large, so it leaves open how much of the failure comes from the basis choice versus the coarse setup.

Which aim should guide the next phase of YM work? I can assess both, but they lead to different recommendations.
- Develop a controlled Wilson-loop hierarchy, while keeping the arithmetic connection in view
- Prioritize a concrete bridge to the Weil-form/RH problem
- Explore the physics first, even if the arithmetic connection remains distant

parts: I found an important limitation in the proposed next-step criterion: the error bound can stay large even when the scalar prediction is exact. It measures the size of discarded components but can miss cancellations in what returns to the readout. I’m also checking lattice-bootstrap work that combines positivity with Yang–Mills loop equations; that may offer a more informative continuation than simply enlarging the curvature basis.

**I would keep the finite-lattice framework, but reconsider the proposed next experiment before expanding it.** The notes establish a useful positive state space. They have not yet established that the chosen hierarchy is an effective way to predict Wilson loops—and the current error bound may be an unnecessarily demanding test of that effectiveness.

I read the four YM notes, the surrounding assessment, and the numerical implementation. I also checked the recorded source hashes and reran the 30 finite-dimensional projection controls; those passed. I did not rerun the Monte Carlo simulation or change any files.

There has actually been **one interacting lattice YM model tested**, alongside several analytical and numerical controls:

| Setting | What it accomplishes | What it leaves unresolved |
|---|---|---|
| Prescribed smooth, noncommuting SU(2) backgrounds; finite SU(3) algebra controls | Tests the continuous curvature equations, moving-basis correction, and residual formulas | Whether those approximations work under a YM measure |
| General finite SU(N) slab with a shared spatial reflection slice | Gives an explicit reflected norm and proves that boundary loop multiplication respects the null-space quotient | Vacuum and continuum limits; useful compression |
| Four-dimensional SU(2), \(6^3\times5\), open time boundaries, \(\beta=1.6\) | Tests the construction under a genuinely interacting Wilson measure | Other couplings, volumes, slab thicknesses, and finer physical resolution |

The one-, two-, and three-observable families are **different approximations within the same lattice theory**, rather than different physical models.

The strongest achievement is the [finite-slab construction](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/susy-positivity/investigations/wilson-loewner/YM/notes/FINITE_SLAB_REFLECTION_AND_DISCRETE_HIERARCHY_20260924.md). Putting the loops on the shared spatial slice allows their multiplication operators to pass through the half-slab integration. That resolves the earlier objection that configuration-wise unitarity need not survive the reflection quotient. Retaining the color channels also gives a precise meaning to the information lost when only the scalar Wilson expectation is observed.

This is a sound foundation for discussing memory and approximation error. But much of the subsequent projection machinery applies to any sequence of unitary boundary observables. **The specifically Yang–Mills challenge is controlling their correlations.** Loewner growth currently chooses the contour sequence; it has not yet supplied a special compression mechanism.

The [interacting experiment](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/susy-positivity/investigations/wilson-loewner/YM/notes/FIRST_INTERACTING_SLAB_TEST_AND_CONTINUATION_20260924.md) is informative precisely because it exposes that distinction. At the middle contour:

| Retained family | Predicted Wilson expectation | Reported output-error bound |
|---|---:|---:|
| Identity | 0.150548 | 0.849452 |
| Identity + curvature probe | 0.135442 | 0.800524 |
| Those + quadratic fluctuation | 0.136709 | 0.798915 |
| Direct measurement | **0.150381 ± 0.000939** | — |

Adding curvature produces a statistically clear error of about 10%, despite capturing more of the state. The quadratic observable barely helps. That is good evidence against continuing by adding powers of this particular averaged chord probe.

It is weaker evidence against a useful hierarchy generally. The actual step distances are roughly \(1.11,1.11,1.40\): these are large changes in the positive norm. A smoothly moving continuum tip does not make its coarse rasterized loop change smoothly. Also, refining the geometric solver without changing the link words provides no new physical resolution.

**My main qualification concerns the proposed requirement that the forward/backward bound fall below 0.01.** It is a sufficient success criterion, but it could reject an excellent scalar approximation because the bound discards essential correlation information.

Here is a simple analytical control. Suppose two independent SU(2) increments satisfy
\[
\mathbb E P_1=\mathbb E P_2=pI.
\]
Then their Wilson expectation is exactly
\[
W_2=\tfrac12\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(P_2P_1)=p^2.
\]
The identity-only approximation therefore gives the exact answer. Yet the notes’ two-step forward/backward estimate is
\[
|W_2-\widehat W_2|\le 1-p^2.
\]
At \(p\approx0.388\), that is approximately **0.849**, even though the actual error is zero—the same scale as the reported scalar bound.

This is not an independence claim about the four-dimensional data. It demonstrates that **large discarded norms need not mean large influence on the output**. The missing components can be large while their relevant pairing vanishes. The bound allows them to align maximally.

That suggests refining the research question to:

> Which omitted correlations can return to the Wilson readout, and what feature of the YM measure controls them?

The exact two-step missing term is
\[
W_2-a_1a_0
=\langle e,\mathcal U_1(I-P)\mathcal U_0e\rangle,
\qquad
a_j=\langle e,\mathcal U_je\rangle.
\]
The current estimate bounds this pairing by the product of two norms. A stronger approach would use dynamics, locality, symmetry, or controlled expansions to constrain the pairing itself. Simply measuring it would diagnose the problem, but would not independently predict \(W_2\).

There is relevant existing work to compare before designing another hierarchy. **Lattice positivity bootstrap combines Wilson-loop Gram positivity with Schwinger–Dyson equations.** For SU(2), trace identities make the equations linear in single-trace loop expectations; the collection of loop shapes remains infinite, so this is not finite closure. Kazakov and Zheng already organize finite families through local loop deformations and obtain numerical bounds in two, three, and four dimensions. [Primary paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16925)

A January 2026 paper also examines relations within a truncated family that appear only after eliminating longer intermediate loops. That is particularly relevant to avoiding an inefficient basis assembled by intuition alone. [Liu and Yang](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.04316)

My assessment is that these methods deserve a focused comparison with the present construction. Their published bounds do not automatically apply to this finite open slab or these particular contours.

For the next phase, I would favor the following bounded sequence:

1. **Calibrate the error criterion in an exactly tractable control.** Independent plaquette increments—or a suitable two-dimensional YM benchmark—can distinguish failure of the approximation from failure of the bound. A two-dimensional benchmark would test the correlation machinery; it would not reproduce the current spatial-slice reflection geometry.

2. **Analyze the smallest nontrivial return-of-memory term.** Use elementary contour deformations and retain their scalar and matrix parts. Determine which loop equations constrain the omitted pairing, and whether they offer information beyond Cauchy–Schwarz. This would make the proposed local-plaquette expansion much more purposeful.

3. **Only then conduct one targeted four-dimensional comparison.** Keep the existing slab as a reference, use a predeclared modest family, and assess output accuracy, uncertainty, and measurement cost on independent chains. The desired result should be either a sharper justified bound or a clear explanation of why the relevant correlations resist compression.

I would defer smoothing until that diagnosis. Slice-only smoothing preserves the boundary construction, which is valuable, but it changes the observable. A successful approximation to a heavily smoothed loop could leave the original difficulty untouched. Likewise, subdividing contour changes alone does not guarantee smaller elementary changes at fixed coupling.

If the immediate objective is **controlled Wilson-loop physics**, this revised lattice route looks worth one carefully bounded investigation. I would retain SU(2) for that test; there is no evidence here that changing gauge group would solve the observed difficulty.

If the immediate objective is **a bridge to the Weil form or RH**, I would give further lattice development lower priority until an independently specified arithmetic pairing emerges. Accurate Wilson-loop predictions would be a physics result, but the current construction supplies neither the required arithmetic coefficients nor an identity with the complete target form.

The choice I would like us to settle first is whether the next result should explain **how YM correlations control the scalar readout**, or establish **an arithmetic identity using the positive space**. The former now has a concrete diagnostic starting point; the latter still needs a candidate dictionary.
Yes lets brainstorm ways to bridge to the Weil form and RH. Can you do an extensive sweep to consider new ideas for how to do that?

I’ll survey possible bridges to the complete Weil form, checking both the project’s earlier attempts and relevant primary literature. I’ll distinguish ideas with a concrete missing identity or inequality from ones that currently offer only an analogy.

A useful distinction is emerging: a direct realization of the Weil quadratic form does not need to reproduce the entire causal zeta transfer function. That opens more possibilities. I’m also checking recent work on arithmetic spectral operators, where primes enter the construction from the outset; the crucial question is what remains unproved between those positive operators and the complete Weil form.

The strongest leads so far start with arithmetic structure already present: semilocal Fourier/Sonin spaces, arithmetic spectral operators, and a possible positivity bootstrap using exact arithmetic relations. I’m also examining a more speculative physical route through Lee–Yang zero-location theorems. None supplies the missing RH argument yet; I’m working out a concrete first test and a clear failure criterion for each.

I found a useful simplification: an established version of Weil’s criterion remains equivalent to RH when tests are constrained so that the two pole terms vanish. That could remove one difficult part of the proposed bridge. The challenge remains to control the prime terms against the archimedean form for arbitrarily large supports.

The existing notes already cover several of the strongest ideas, so I’m separating refinements from genuinely different directions. One useful reframing is to write the prime terms as positive jump energies minus their exact diagonal cost. This gives an arithmetic random-walk model, but the required sharp inequality remains unproved. Lee–Yang theory offers a more distinct physical route, through zero-location theorems rather than Weil-form positivity.

I’m organizing the sweep into three choices: a direct Sonin-form comparison, an arithmetic positivity bootstrap inspired by the YM work, and a Lee–Yang feasibility study. I also found a specific correction worth recording: prime-power logarithms are locally finite, not dense, so adding more unscaled prime lattices cannot by itself produce the continuous gamma kernel.

I completed the sweep and saved a [detailed research note](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/susy-positivity/investigations/wilson-loewner/notes/ARITHMETIC_BRIDGE_SWEEP_AFTER_YM_20260924.md). It examines six routes in depth, screens ten others, and links 20 primary sources.

**My recommendation is to make the next investigation arithmetic from the outset.** The YM work contributes useful methods—positive Gram matrices, exact equations, careful adjoints, and projection estimates—but we still need a structure that explains the primes and their exact coefficients. Enlarging the current lattice does not presently address that missing connection.

Some leading ideas already appear in your notes. The sweep mainly sharpens their targets, while identifying a few meaningfully different alternatives.

The most useful simplification is that an RH proof need not first realize the unrestricted Weil form physically. One can restrict compactly supported tests to

\[
\int e^{x/2}f(x)\,dx=\int e^{-x/2}f(x)\,dx=0.
\]

Both pole terms then vanish, and positivity on this class **for all support lengths** remains equivalent to RH. This follows from the prescribed-vanishing version of Weil’s criterion. [Connes–Consani, Appendix C](https://arxiv.org/html/2006.13771v1).

That changes what we need to build: the gamma–prime comparison remains, but constructing the signed pole sectors can be deferred.

| Route | What makes it promising | What remains unproved |
|---|---|---|
| **Semilocal Sonin comparison** | Arithmetic scaling and Fourier duality already provide a canonical positive pairing. | A signed bound comparing that pairing with the restricted Weil form. |
| **Arithmetic positivity bootstrap** | Transfers the strongest YM methodology: positivity combined with exact operator identities. | An independently defined arithmetic state and identities that force the required coefficients and cancellations. |
| **Arithmetic jump-energy model** | Rewrites the actual Weil form as positive jump energies minus an explicit diagonal cost. | A sharp constrained Poincaré inequality, valid for every support length. |
| **Screw-function / no-crossing approach** | Replaces the distributional form with a continuous kernel and finite-interval operators. | Excluding the first zero eigenvalue as the interval grows. |
| **Arithmetic spectral approximants** | Existing constructions produce self-adjoint operators and real-zero entire functions. | Convergence strong enough to identify the entire limit with \(\Xi\), including its possible nonreal zeros. |
| **Lee–Yang statistical mechanics** | Offers a different physical mechanism that directly constrains zero locations. | A rigorous representation or approximation of the theta kernel within a Lee–Yang class. |

The first three deserve the closest discussion.

**1. The Sonin route is the strongest immediate continuation.**

These spaces already combine arithmetic operations with ordinary Hilbert-space positivity. Their place-adjoining maps change the metric, however, so compatibility of the spaces does not establish the needed inequality. [Connes–Consani–Moscovici](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.18423v1).

Your earlier comparison has the right structure:

\[
Q_L[f]=B_{S,L}[f]+R_{S,L}[f],
\qquad B_{S,L}[f]\ge0.
\]

The next question is whether the **actual arithmetic remainder** satisfies \(R_{S,L}\ge-B_{S,L}\), first on the pole-neutral source class.

This is more focused than asking for an entire new physical theory. It also has an informative failure outcome: a controlled counterexample could rule out that particular comparison without ruling out Weil positivity.

I would begin by independently auditing the existing projection formula and its domains, then testing the complete signed remainder. Another arbitrary positive matrix would not answer this question.

**2. An arithmetic bootstrap is the most interesting way to reuse the YM work.**

The essential lesson from lattice bootstrapping is that positivity becomes restrictive when combined with exact dynamics and algebraic identities. [Kazakov–Zheng](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16925).

For arithmetic, a simple starting point is

\[
V_n|m\rangle=|nm\rangle,\qquad H|m\rangle=(\log m)|m\rangle,
\]

so that

\[
[H,V_n]=(\log n)V_n.
\]

Here logarithms arise from the arithmetic action itself. But these operators alone do not supply the Weil form: a real-place Fourier or Poisson constraint, and the appropriate state, remain essential.

A good first target would be **one exact two-prime identity** explaining something the previous models could not:

- why repetitions of a prime retain the primitive weight \(\log p\);
- why the central form has a contribution at \(\log4\), but none at \(\log6\);
- why a shared construction does not leave an unwanted correlation at \(\log(3/2)\).

Such an identity would justify building a hierarchy. Without it, a larger optimization risks encoding the desired answer into its assumptions.

**3. A different lattice model could represent arithmetic jump energies directly.**

The elementary identity

\[
-2c\,\operatorname{Re}\langle F,U_dF\rangle
=c\|F-U_dF\|^2-2c\|F\|^2
\]

turns every prime term into a positive jump energy with its compulsory diagonal subtraction.

On the pole-neutral class, the target therefore becomes

\[
Q_L[f]=\mathcal E_L[F]-\kappa_L\|F\|^2,
\]

where \(\mathcal E_L\) contains the continuous gamma jump kernel and jumps at the exact prime-power logarithms.

This suggests an arithmetic random-walk model with a precise purpose: prove the required constrained spectral-gap inequality. **Positivity of the jump energy alone accomplishes too little.** The exact diagonal cost is the difficulty that previous independent-prime constructions encountered. The possible new ingredient would be a Fourier/Poisson uncertainty estimate that controls it.

This is worth considering as an analytic companion to the Sonin route, rather than immediately launching another simulation.

Two further alternatives deserve attention, with different tradeoffs.

The **screw-function approach** could focus the problem on excluding a first null mode as support grows. Suzuki’s work provides the continuous-kernel and operator framework; it does not supply the global no-crossing argument. [Suzuki, 2026](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.09096v2). I would investigate whether the null equation admits a specific arithmetic boundary identity.

The **Lee–Yang route** is the clearest fresh physical direction. Instead of identifying \(Q\) with a norm, seek ferromagnetic partition functions whose transforms converge to \(\Xi\). A valid zero-location theorem could then imply RH and hence Weil positivity. Positive probability weights are insufficient: the interaction hypotheses and convergence of entire functions must be established. The connection to the theta kernel and de Bruijn–Newman deformation is substantial existing mathematics. [Newman–Wu](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.06596).

The spectral-triple route is also serious, but its positive quotient is formed after subtracting the lowest eigenvalue. That does not establish positivity of the original Weil matrix; the missing convergence theorem remains central. [Connes–Consani–Moscovici, Theorem 5.10](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.22755v1).

**My preferred next assignment would be the restricted Sonin comparison**, with the arithmetic bootstrap as a possible source of new identities. If you want a substantially different physical principle, I would choose a bounded Lee–Yang feasibility study. Those choices give us concrete mathematical questions to settle before investing in a larger model or computation.

I am drawn to the second approach, an arithmetic bootstrap. Before proceeding, please provide a deeper explanation of this proposal, what it needs to accomplish, ideas that have been tried, difficulties to overcome, and proposed next steps.

I’ll examine what an arithmetic bootstrap would actually constrain, which ingredients already exist, and where it risks assuming the positivity it is meant to prove. I’ll connect that to the earlier attempts and outline a first investigation with a clear success or failure criterion.

The key gap is becoming clearer: positive arithmetic states and exact prime-weight identities already exist, including in your Bost–Connes note. What is missing is an identity coupling those arithmetic correlations to the gamma contribution in the same positive pairing. I also found that a naive thermal Gram matrix of the multiplication operators loses the cross terms through stationarity, so that simplest version would be too weak.

A useful distinction is emerging between two versions of the proposal. One would bootstrap the actual Weil operator using correlations of shifted inputs and Fourier operators; the other would construct a larger arithmetic state whose norm realizes that operator. The first gives us a concrete diagnostic for the second. In either version, mixed correlations such as the one at \(\log(3/2)\) belong in the auxiliary matrices, even though their coefficients must cancel from the final Weil form.

I would sharpen the first milestone: recovering prime-power weights or cancelling composite terms is already possible through Euler-product and Möbius identities. Progress would mean using those identities to control the joint gamma–prime quadratic form, including its exact diagonal term. I’m putting the proposed steps in that order: specify the objects, derive a useful joint identity, then consider a small optimization.

**The arithmetic bootstrap is worth investigating, but its central task is still to find the right equations.** We already have positive arithmetic states, exact prime coefficients, and positive Gram matrices. What we lack is an identity that makes those ingredients constrain the **combined gamma–prime Weil form**.

That sharpens my earlier proposal: reproducing prime-power weights or cancelling composite coefficients would be calibration. The new accomplishment must connect those arithmetic identities to the required positivity.

I saved the fuller mathematical specification in [Arithmetic bootstrap: design and open gaps](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/susy-positivity/investigations/wilson-loewner/notes/ARITHMETIC_BOOTSTRAP_DESIGN_AND_OPEN_GAPS_20260924.md).

**A bootstrap would extract consequences from positivity and exact identities together.**

Choose observables \(A_1,\ldots,A_N\) in an independently defined positive state \(\varphi\). Their correlation matrix satisfies

\[
M_{ij}=\varphi(A_i^*A_j)\succeq0,
\]

because every linear combination obeys

\[
\varphi\!\left[\left(\sum_i c_iA_i\right)^*
                    \left(\sum_j c_jA_j\right)\right]\ge0.
\]

Positivity alone allows many possible correlations. Algebraic relations, equilibrium identities, Fourier duality, and support conditions restrict them further.

In a lattice bootstrap, loop equations provide much of this additional information. Increasing the observable family then makes the consistency conditions more restrictive. [Kazakov–Zheng](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16925v2).

For arithmetic, the intended progression is:

1. Specify genuine arithmetic and Fourier operators.
2. Derive identities their correlations must satisfy.
3. Express the Weil form using those correlations.
4. Find its lowest possible value subject to the valid constraints.
5. Extract a verifiable inequality explaining the bound.

The coefficients of the Weil form are already known. The bootstrap’s purpose is to explain their joint sign.

A desirable result would look schematically like

\[
Q_L[f]
=\sum_j\|B_jf\|^2
+\underbrace{\text{terms vanishing by exact identities}}_{0}
+\text{controlled remainder}.
\]

A finite numerical optimization could help discover such a decomposition. The mathematical certificate—and its treatment of the remainder—is what would count.

**There is a concrete version of this idea that starts directly with the Weil operator.**

Let \(F\) be a normalized input supported in an interval of length \(L\), and define

\[
z_q=\langle F,U_{\log q}F\rangle,
\qquad U_aF(x)=F(x-a).
\]

The three vectors \(F,U_{\log2}F,U_{\log3}F\) give the positive matrix

\[
\begin{pmatrix}
1&z_2&z_3\\
\overline{z_2}&1&z_{3/2}\\
\overline{z_3}&\overline{z_{3/2}}&1
\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.
\]

The entry \(z_{3/2}\) follows from composing the translations. Support supplies another exact condition:

\[
z_q=0\qquad\text{when }|\log q|\ge L.
\]

On the pole-neutral source class discussed previously, the objective is

\[
Q_L[F]
=K_\Gamma[F]+w_0
-2\sum_{m\log p<L}(\log p)p^{-m/2}\operatorname{Re}z_{p^m}.
\]

This makes the proposed optimization tangible: constrain the arithmetic correlations and the gamma expectation **for the same input**.

Two details are crucial.

First, \(z_{3/2}\) is a legitimate auxiliary correlation. Its absence from the final Weil formula does **not** mean it should be set to zero. Its coefficient must disappear from the completed objective, while the correlation can help constrain the other entries.

Second, estimating each \(|z_q|\) separately throws away the joint information. Retaining that information is the main potential advantage over the norm-product estimates that proved weak in the YM experiment.

**There are two related research programs here, with different burdens.**

| Version | What is independently available | What must be discovered |
|---|---|---|
| **Bootstrap the actual Weil operator** | The input Hilbert space, translations, gamma operator, support restrictions, and target form | Strong enough joint constraints or a reusable positivity certificate |
| **Construct an arithmetic realization** | Positive arithmetic algebras and states, such as Bost–Connes or semilocal Fourier constructions | A source map whose positive pairing equals or controls the Weil form |

The first version is more concrete and can diagnose proposed identities. The second offers the deeper physical interpretation envisioned in my earlier sketch.

I would connect them: investigate an arithmetic realization, but express its proposed contribution as a precise constraint on the actual Weil operator. This gives us a way to tell whether the construction adds useful information.

**Several important ingredients have already been obtained.**

Your [Bost–Connes investigation](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/susy-positivity/investigations/wilson-loewner/WZW/notes/ARITHMETIC_ORBIT_WEIGHTS_AND_BOST_CONNES_TEST_20260923.md) goes substantially beyond merely observing that a partition function is \(\zeta\).

For multiplication operators \(V_n|m\rangle=|nm\rangle\), their range projections \(e_n=V_nV_n^*\) satisfy divisibility relations. The equilibrium state gives

\[
\varphi_\beta(e_n)=n^{-\beta}.
\]

Thus even the central prime coefficient has an exact arithmetic-state expression:

\[
(\log p)p^{-m/2}
=(\log p)\varphi_{1/2}(e_{p^m}).
\]

Positive equilibrium states in this temperature range exist independently; they do not require a convergent ordinary Gibbs trace. [Neshveyev](https://arxiv.org/html/0907.1456).

The obstacle is therefore more specific than “find a positive arithmetic state.” It is to connect that state to the required source correlations and gamma contribution.

Other attempted constructions clarify the problem:

| Previous idea | What worked | What remained wrong or missing |
|---|---|---|
| Independent prime delay squares | Produce the desired negative cross terms inside positive norms | Also produce compulsory positive diagonal terms |
| Coherent multi-prime amplitudes | Put several primes in one positive space | Introduce additional mixed-ratio terms |
| Euler partition functions and logarithmic derivatives | Give correct repetitions and remove mixed composites | The logarithmic derivative is not automatically a positive quadratic form |
| Semilocal Fourier/Sonin spaces | Supply canonical arithmetic maps and positive norms | Leave a signed comparison remainder |
| Schur elimination and finite-window certificates | Establish rigorous local inequalities | Do not supply an all-length continuation mechanism |

These are scoped limitations, documented in the [failure inventory](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/susy-positivity/brainstorm/candidate-bulk-theories/FAILURES.md), rather than exclusions of every possible bootstrap.

For example, the identity

\[
-\partial_s\log\frac1{(1-2^{-s})(1-3^{-s})}
=
\sum_{m\ge1}(\log2)2^{-ms}
+\sum_{m\ge1}(\log3)3^{-ms}
\]

already explains both the repeated-prime weight and the absence of a mixed \(6^{-s}\) term. The bootstrap needs to make this arithmetic cancellation participate in a **positive completed pairing**.

**A simple calculation also rules out the most naive thermal Gram construction.**

In an equilibrium state invariant under

\[
\sigma_t(V_n)=n^{it}V_n,
\]

we have

\[
\varphi(V_m^*V_n)
=(n/m)^{it}\varphi(V_m^*V_n).
\]

For \(m\ne n\), invariance for every \(t\) forces the expectation to vanish. Therefore

\[
\varphi(V_m^*V_n)=\delta_{mn}.
\]

A source built merely as \(\sum_n a_n(f)V_n\) has norm \(\sum_n|a_n(f)|^2\). The different arithmetic labels do not interfere.

This does not exclude the full arithmetic algebra. It tells us that the bare multiplication operators are too small a family. We need a different preparation, additional operators, or a coupled real-place construction. One possibility is a composite observable whose arithmetic and real-place flow weights balance, allowing cross correlations to survive. That remains a construction to derive.

The input-state Gram matrix above is unaffected by this limitation: an arbitrary compactly supported input is not a thermal invariant state.

**The most plausible source of the missing equations is the interaction between arithmetic scaling and additive Fourier structure.**

The multiplication relations alone are quite generic. Similar relations can be built for prime-labelled oscillators with assigned energies. They do not explain why those energies fit the gamma factor.

The richer arithmetic algebra includes additive characters and divisibility projectors. Semilocal constructions also provide exact intertwining between real and finite-place Fourier transforms and scaling operations. [Connes–Consani–Moscovici](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.18423v1).

I would look for an identity containing both kinds of operators that does one of the following:

- constrains a troublesome arithmetic cross correlation using real-place information;
- accounts for the exact diagonal terms introduced by completing squares;
- controls the signed remainder between a canonical positive pairing and \(Q_L\).

Borrowing these operators does not commit us to the earlier Sonin domination proposal. They could instead provide the algebra for a bootstrap.

**The difficulties are structural as well as computational.**

The most serious ones are:

- **Circularity.** Requiring the Weil matrix itself to be positive, or assuming the desired norm identity, cannot serve as an input constraint.
- **Weak relaxations.** A negative optimization bound may come from artificial moment assignments that no genuine input realizes. It does not refute Weil positivity.
- **Incorrect truncation.** Finite moment matrices can describe infinite-dimensional operators. Finite square matrices cannot exactly represent proper isometries: \(V^*V=I\) would force \(VV^*=I\). Hard occupation cutoffs therefore introduce boundary defects.
- **Domains and tails.** The gamma operator and logarithmic generators are unbounded. Their approximation errors must remain in the inequality.
- **Critical accuracy.** Your prime-weight tests show why a small unexplained diagonal or coefficient change can matter.
- **Global scope.** Success for a finite source family or several intervals does not establish positivity for every compactly supported input.

General noncommutative optimization theory supplies useful hierarchy and certificate machinery under suitable boundedness assumptions. Applying it here requires proving that our operators, constraints, and limits meet the relevant hypotheses. [Pironio–Navascués–Acín](https://arxiv.org/html/0903.4368).

**I would propose the following next steps, before any substantial numerical campaign.**

1. **Write the exact bootstrap specification.** Fix the pole-neutral source class, operators, adjoints, state, and objective. Separate established identities from conjectural ones. The objective must be explicitly expressible in the selected moments.

2. **Build the smallest faithful examples.** Start with primes \(2\) and \(3\), their ratio correlations, shared gamma observables, and support constraints. For the auxiliary arithmetic construction, retain additive-character and divisibility relations. Use existing coefficient identities as calibration.

3. **Demand one informative joint identity.** It must involve the real-place and arithmetic sectors and yield a consequence beyond separate positivity. This is the main research milestone.

4. **Only then formulate a small optimization.** Compare the bound before and after adding that identity. Check the prime-square regime at \(L>\log4\). Test composite cancellation algebraically before support truncation, or beyond \(\log6\) with prime \(5\) included; below that threshold, support would hide the coefficient automatically.

5. **Extract and verify the mathematical result.** Seek a symbolic identity, rigorous improvement, or controlled obstruction. Continue only if it exposes a mechanism that could extend beyond the particular finite matrix.

My preference is to define the next investigation around **one joint arithmetic–Fourier identity and its consequence for the Weil form**. That would make this a substantive new direction while giving us an early way to distinguish progress from a more elaborate restatement of the original positivity problem.
